provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The constructor writes output[size-1-c][r] = grid[r][c]. That is a whole-grid 90 degree counter-clockwise rotation, and every colour, including the background, keeps its value. Under a D4 transform g, the visible rule becomes g T g^-1. Rotations commute with rotations, so d4 values 0 to 3 keep the counter-clockwise rotation. Reflections (d4 values 4 to 7) conjugate a counter-clockwise rotation into a clockwise one, because F R^-1 F = R and R^k R R^-k = R. The emitted program builds the rotated grid directly with an explicit index map in visible coordinates. For counter-clockwise it uses out[i][j] = g[j][W-1-i]. For clockwise it uses out[i][j] = g[H-1-j][i]. The output shape is W by H, so rectangular grids also work. The program never changes a colour, so the palette permutation needs no special handling.
draft_notes.limitations: The constructor only produces square 3x3 grids that use one colour on a 0 background. The emitted rule is a pure geometric rotation, so it is independent of colour and size and also handles rectangular inputs. The demonstrations are not consulted because the direction is fixed by d4. I found no constructor defects or fixture contradictions, and all approved fixtures match a counter-clockwise rotation at d4 = 0. No tests were run.

independent_source_review.mechanism: The whole grid is rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise in the native frame. The constructor writes `output[size-1-c][r] = grid[r][c]`, so input cell (r,c) moves to output (W-1-c, r). That is `np.rot90(k=1)`, the same as the archived program. Colours, including the background, are carried over unchanged. Under a D4 augmentation g, the visible rule is g·R·g⁻¹. Rotations commute with R, so it stays counter-clockwise. Reflections conjugate R into R⁻¹, which is clockwise. The factory selects clockwise when d4 ≥ 4.
evidence: Constructor line `output[size - 1 - c][r] = grid[r][c]` maps (r,c) to (W-1-c, r). The factory's counter-clockwise body `out[i][j] = g[j][W-1-i]` is the same map: with i = W-1-c and j = r it reads g[r][c].
Factory clockwise body `out[i][j] = g[H-1-j][i]` with output shape W×H is a correct clockwise rotation (`np.rot90(k=-1)`). It is the inverse of the counter-clockwise map.

Conjugation check: for a reflection F, F·R·F = R⁻¹. For a rotation S, S·R·S⁻¹ = R. So branching on whether d4 is a reflection is correct, assuming indices 4–7 are reflections. The host audit passed with d4 = 7 across 8000 augmented checks, which is consistent with this assumption.

Approved fixtures, checked by hand: train 1 rows come from the columns right to left: 999 / 009 / 009, which matches. The test input columns read right to left give 005 / 005 / 050, which matches. Pairs 2–4 also follow the counter-clockwise rotation.

The constructor's validate() inputs reproduce the canonical fixture inputs, in a different order. Train 1 in validate() is fixture 4, for example. They are generated by the same index map, so the fixtures and the constructor agree.
No hidden latent decides the label. The output is a deterministic function of the visible input. Colour and pixel positions are visible, and the colour is copied unchanged.

The emitted solver uses explicit index maps in augmented visible coordinates. It does not untransform the grid, solve natively and retransform. The rotation is the puzzle operation itself, which is legitimate.
The palette is irrelevant because no colour is ever mapped. The background remains the generated 0, which becomes palette[0] after permutation, and it rotates with everything else.
nonblocking_limits: The constructor only produces 3×3 grids with a single colour on background 0, using 2–8 pixels. The solver is more general: it handles any colour and rectangular shapes.

Demonstrations are not consulted. The rotation direction is a deterministic spatial constant fixed by d4, which is allowed. Some sampled episodes may contain symmetric demos that would also fit a different D4 map, but the generator's label is still unambiguous.

The reflection/rotation partition of d4 (0–3 rotations, 4–7 reflections) is inferred from the factory comment and the host audit's pass at d4 = 7. I did not verify it against the augmentation module source.

draft_notes.host_review: Explicit visible index rotation; augmentation source confirms d4>=4 is a reflection and d4%4 counts clockwise quarter turns, so conjugation reverses CCW only under reflections. Builder demonstrations_disambiguate checks symmetric-demo conflicts.
